recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements: the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Name: LotusWei Flower Elixirs
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Offer Line: Use my affiliate link to support InnerVerse

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recLy5DrjiTT1fS5p.Bio: Benjamin Balderson is a practicing alchemist who has taught laboratory (practical) alchemy on InnerVerse, covering distillation, alcohol-free tinctures, and the alchemical patterns found in nature; he shares his work under the banner "Odin's Alchemy."
recLy5DrjiTT1fS5p.Name: Benjamin Balderson

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Purpose as the core of masculine energy", "body": "Chance argued that the heart of masculine energy was knowing a purpose and pursuing it relentlessly, while feminine energy supported that pursuit, and he said the same dance had to happen inside each person before it showed up between two people. He claimed that factory work and later entertainment pulled men away from purpose. Chance also described attraction as a kind of vibe check on that purpose, and he suggested that confusing money or status with purpose led to trouble on both sides. Michelle and Rachel added their own views on balance."}, {"title": "The masculine role and online culture", "body": "Chance described a corner of online commentary that spent its energy pointing out the supposed mental illness of the opposing political side, and he called that a corruption of the masculine role. In his view, the true masculine would build something better instead of fighting pointless verbal battles. He also equated left and right politics with masculine and feminine, and he stressed that every person carried both. Rachel replied that she felt a mismatch with some stereotypes of femininity, and Michelle said she related, adding that society portrayed the roles differently than she had experienced them."}, {"title": "Patriarchy, Webster's 1828, and word warfare", "body": "One participant asked what patriarchy actually meant and whether anyone had really seen it. One of the hosts then read the 1828 Webster's definitions of patriarch and patriarchy as rule by a father over a family, and reported that the dictionary had no entry for matriarchy. That host wondered aloud whether the divide was a later tactic of word warfare. Another speaker wondered whether the term was shaped by church imagery, noting how the Hierophant tarot card is usually drawn and that some newer decks softened that imagery."}, {"title": "Nature as a teacher of polarity", "body": "Kyle described the elder tree as a feminine archetype of the fairy world and the hawthorn as its masculine counterpart, and he explained how scent works as a subtle psychoactive switch. He said incense carried a fiery masculine principle while hydrosols carried a watery feminine one. Michelle told of thanking a branch on a hike and seeing a gentleman offering a hand as a sign of the divine masculine and feminine. Chance told a story about a beaver felled tree that became a resting place for turtles, reading the beaver as masculine and the turtles as feminine."}, {"title": "Beauty, balance, and the luminaries", "body": "Chance argued that objective beauty, like a flower in bloom, worked as a guide, and that refusing to call ugly things beautiful would help people detox their lives. He pointed to a swordsman who was also a poet as a picture of both poles being strong at once. Rachel described the sun and moon as a way for light and dark to communicate, and she said women's cycles tracking the moon could be a gentle language between the sexes. Michelle encouraged men not to give up and to work on themselves, since that was how they attracted partners."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Rachel Munoz and Michelle Lundquist join Vibe Rant tonight to talk about mastering masculine energy, from the feminine perspective. If you want the Valkyries to carry you to Valhalla, be sure to warrior up and tune in!
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The masculine wouldn't go and fight verbal fights and bully the side that they say are the bullies. The real true masculine would not engage in fights that were pointless. They would just build something better, build something outside of that, show the truth through action rather than spitting acid at all the people that they think are the problem.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Because when you have both in their roles, this is why my project is called Healing Home. You create a place of healing. Your home becomes your altar of a place for all sorts of healing to happen.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "In my opinion, this is a dynamic that exists because it's part of the female role of vibe checking the masculine. And if the masculine is really off purpose and not pursuing purpose as they should be, then they're going to be less and less attractive to the feminine.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you smell something aromatic, it puts you into a different state of mind. So it's just a real subtle psychoactive switch in your mind.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You had the camaraderie of a team of men. We replaced that with sports ball like Chance keeps talking about where now sports ball is your team, your guys. And if they win, you win.", "author": "Benjamin Balderson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9076d077-da2c-4992-abc8-c4cc7575dc14/BENJAMIN-BALDERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But I think that the incense has more of like, you know, it's going straight up, it's going to heaven. It's got the fiery masculine principle, the hydrosol has got the watery feminine principle. And it's really fun to work with both of those and then to feel those together in the field.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's like what you're describing might look androgynous, but it's really like both of the poles of the dynamic disequilibrium are strong and distinct in the being. He is a swordsman and a poet, a gentleman and a scholar, all of these things.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If we really get real with ourself about what is and isn't beautiful and we don't lie to ourself about it, and we structure our life in a way to bring about as much beauty into ourself on all sensory levels as possible, and either fix and bring back to balance or create boundaries against that which is not beautiful, we will be detoxing ourself on a lot of levels.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And then I thought about just the gesture of a gentleman who offers his hand to a woman to allow her to pass over a rocky area or a puddle or whatever it be, and it was just this beautiful spark that I had of, oh my gosh, this to me is an example that nature is giving me of this divine masculine feminine connection that's there and it's everywhere.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think you're right. Both of you, Kyle and Michelle, when you start to interact with spirit, you see these dynamics that we're talking about play out in such a natural way. You just see it. It's so clear and it's so obvious and it's so beautiful to watch it interact, and you can learn from it so easily.", "author": "Rachel Munoz", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So the turtles in the metaphor are the feminine. They're even circular, they have a shell, they carry their home with them, a lot of reasons why you can correlate that. And by the masculine fulfilling its purpose, not even necessarily knowing why it's fulfilling its purpose, it's just doing what it's called to do, then the feminine builds a home out of that.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's, let's work together. Let's get your chaos in a way that I can understand it. I know, now that you're going to go through this and here's your peak time, here's your low time. I understand your flow now. I get it. It's a way that we can communicate and understand each other and it's right there. It's not even complicated.", "author": "Rachel Munoz", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "When I learned about this, I'm like, wow, that's kind of brutal. And I guess a message to a man that might be trapped in that cycle of thinking is that there's women out there that want to create this beauty with you.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
